page: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v6 is a low-memory, local disk-enabled virtual machine instance powered by Microsoft Hyper-V. It is built on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at up to 4.2 GHz. The instance offers 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 KB of L1 data cache. Advanced instruction set support includes AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and modern cryptographic acceleration via AES and VAES.

The hardware configuration features 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU. While classed historically within the broader D-family, this configuration aligns structurally with compute-optimized ratios due to lower relative memory sizing. Integrated local storage provides 5,670 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity, offering direct fast scratch space alongside support for premium storage disks. The instance contains no bundled GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes show top-tier multi-threaded processing. The instance placed in the top 10% on Geekbench multi-core (21,105.0) and PassMark CPU (86,003.68), alongside top-tier results in static web serving throughput (110.74 GB/sec) and Geekbench image processing. Multi-core stress-ng tests reached 79,833.5, and memory bandwidth achieved 247.62 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads. In-memory Redis SET operations demonstrated strong performance at 100.88 million operations per second.

Given its compute-heavy 1:2 memory ratio and substantial 5,670 GB local NVMe SSD capacity, the D96lds_v6 provides strong hardware density for parallel processing without the cost overhead of high-memory tiers. It is well matched for software compilation, high-volume batch processing, CI/CD pipelines, static web serving clusters, and multi-threaded ETL jobs where local ephemeral high-speed storage is required.

Structured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation, the system provides 192.0 GB of RAM alongside 5,670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, with no integrated GPUs. Hardware extensions include AVX-512 and AMX for accelerated matrix and vector computation. In benchmarks, the instance achieves top 10% rankings in Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU metrics, paired with 110.74 GB/sec static web throughput and strong multi-threaded decompression rates.
